title: Suricata
subtitle: Inspect traffic and record matches. Tell Suricata which addresses are yours, then download rules.
unsupportedTitle: This device does not include Suricata
unsupportedBody: Intrusion detection is not available on the connected router. Switch to a device that includes it to configure watched interfaces, your network, and logging.
removeSuricataHelp: Stops inspection and deletes the interfaces, groups, and logging configured here. Downloaded rules are left on the router.
removeSuricataDescription: The router will stop inspecting traffic. This does not delete rules that were already downloaded.
discardUnsavedDescription: Refresh reloads Suricata from the router and drops the edits on this page.
addressEntryError: Use an address or network prefix, such as 10.1.0.0/16. A prefix must be the network address, not a host inside it.
portEntryError: Use a port from 1 to 65535, or a range such as 1000-1005.
entryAlreadyInGroup: That entry is already in the group.
invalidGroupName: Name the group with lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. Rules will see it as a variable.
groupNameExists: A group with that name already exists.
nameBecomesVariable: The name becomes the variable rules match against.
excludeThisAddress: Exclude this address instead of including it
excludeThisPort: Exclude this port instead of including it
nameGroupToPreview: Name the group to see the variable.
groupStillUsed: {name} is still used by {groups}. Edit those groups first.
prefixMustBeNetwork: Use an address or a network prefix. A prefix must be the network address.
entryAlreadyInNetwork: That entry is already in your network.
externalNetDefault: $EXTERNAL_NET is everything that is not your network.
externalNetMissing: $EXTERNAL_NET is not defined. Rules for outside addresses will not match.
homeNetMissing: Your network is not defined. Rules look for $HOME_NET.
addNetworkAndStandard: Add your network and the standard groups
variableSummary: {addressCount, plural, one {# address group} other {# address groups}} and {portCount, plural, one {# port group} other {# port groups}}. Downloaded rules match these names. Renaming a standard group stops those rules from matching.
fileNameHint: Leave this blank to use eve.json. A bare name is written under /var/log/suricata/. An absolute path is used as-is.
loggingOff: Logging is off. Suricata can still inspect traffic, but matches will not be recorded here.
rulesBody: Rules are not edited on this page. After this configuration is saved, the router downloads them with <mono>update suricata</mono>. That command is not available through the device API, so run it from the router CLI, or schedule <mono>/usr/libexec/vyos/op_mode/update_suricata.sh</mono> under <scheduler>System Settings, Task Scheduler</scheduler>. The download also restarts Suricata. It does nothing until this service is saved.
deleteGroupDescription: Rules that use {variable} will stop matching. This is not saved until you save the page.
purposeHomeNet: Addresses you own. Rules call this $HOME_NET.
purposeExternalNet: Everything that is not your network.
purposeHttpServers: Web servers. Defaults to your network.
purposeSmtpServers: Mail servers. Defaults to your network.
purposeSqlServers: Database servers. Defaults to your network.
purposeDnsServers: DNS servers. Defaults to your network.
purposeTelnetServers: Telnet servers. Defaults to your network.
purposeAimServers: Legacy messaging servers. Defaults to outside your network.
purposeDcServers: Domain controllers. Defaults to your network.
purposeDnp3Server: DNP3 servers. Defaults to your network.
purposeDnp3Client: DNP3 clients. Defaults to your network.
purposeModbusClient: Modbus clients. Defaults to your network.
purposeModbusServer: Modbus servers. Defaults to your network.
purposeEnipClient: EtherNet/IP clients. Defaults to your network.
purposeEnipServer: EtherNet/IP servers. Defaults to your network.
purposeShellcodePorts: Ports excluded from shellcode rules. Defaults to not port 80.
interfaceNameError: Use a router interface name such as eth0, eth0.10, or bond0.
inspectedNotBlocked: Traffic on these interfaces is inspected. This does not block it.
prefixError: Use a network prefix, such as 192.0.2.0/24. A host address belongs in a group after setup.
addAtLeastOnePrefix: Add at least one prefix for your network.
stepInterfacesBody: Suricata inspects traffic on the interfaces you select. It does not sit inline, and it does not drop packets from this page.
stepNetworkBody: These prefixes become $HOME_NET. Everything else becomes $EXTERNAL_NET. Replace the private ranges if they are not the networks you actually use. Add IPv6 prefixes if you need them.
createStandardVariablesHelp: Adds the address and port names downloaded rules look for, such as web servers and SSH. Your network is always created so those rules can match it. The three capture port groups are always created because this device will not start Suricata without them.
recordRuleMatchesHelp: Writes alerts to eve.json. You can add connection and protocol logs after setup.
viewOnly: You can view this page, but not change it.
